blocks.title: Network architecture
blocks.text: Network architecture is the overall design of a computer network: how computers, servers and other devices are arranged, and how data is transmitted across the network.
Network architecture includes the hardware, the software and the communication rules. A good architecture helps the network work efficiently and supports its future expansion (Fig 1.2).

blocks.alt: An Internet cloud at the top is wired to a wireless router with Wi-Fi waves; from the router a branching cable runs down to a desktop computer, a laptop, a server rack, a tablet and a printer.
blocks.caption: Figure 1.2: Network architecture shows how devices and components are organized in a network (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 1.2).

items: The data is broken into small units called packets for transmission.
The packets travel through cables or wireless signals.
Network devices guide each packet to the correct destination.
The receiving device reassembles the packets into the original data.

blocks.text: This process allows smooth and fast communication.

blocks.title: Class activity
blocks.text: Look at pictures or names of devices and match each device name with its function; then discuss the answers.
